data.title: Campaign Targets a Defined Audience Segment
data.summary:
Campaign content is addressed to a specific, consistently selected audience rather than
a general public. Language, platform choice and timing all narrow onto the same segment,
which indicates deliberate audience selection rather than organic spread.
data.description:
Organic controversy is untidy: it reaches whoever happens to encounter it, in whatever
words they use themselves. A planned operation is tidier, and that tidiness is the
indicator. Where a narrative appears in one language register, on the platforms one
group uses, at the hours that group is awake, the selection was made before the content
was written.

Identifying the audience matters more than identifying the author. It tells the client
who is being worked on, which determines where a correction would have to land to be
seen, and it usually reveals the objective: an operation aimed at a workforce is after
something different from one aimed at customers or at a regulator.

Record the evidence for the segmentation — the platform mix, the vocabulary, the timing
distribution — rather than asserting it. Audience selection is an inference, and it
should be presented with the confidence the evidence supports.
data.recommendation:
* Identify which of the client's own audiences overlaps the targeted segment, and brief
  that audience directly rather than issuing a general statement.
* Monitor the platforms the segment actually uses, which are frequently not the ones the
  communications team watches.
* Where the targeted segment is the client's own staff, route the briefing through
  internal channels before anything is said publicly.
data.short_recommendation: Brief the targeted segment directly, on the platforms it uses.
